structure:Codelist.common:Name: Financial Soundness Indicators (FSI), Balance Sheet and Income Statement Analysis Stocks, Transactions, Other Flows

structure:Code.common:Name: Total assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of nonfinancial and financial assets, representing the total resources owned by the institutional unit.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Economic assets that are financial instruments - representing financial claims arising from contractual relationships created when one institutional unit provides funds or other resources to another.

structure:Code.common:Name: Currency and deposits
structure:Code.common:Description: Currency comprises notes and coins of fixed nominal values, issued or authorized by the central bank or government. Deposits represent the placements of funds that are available for withdrawal on demand or within a short period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt securities
structure:Code.common:Description: Negotiable financial instruments that represent a claim on the issuer and give the holder an unconditional right to receive interest and/or principal payments�such as bills, bonds and debentures, commercial paper, negotiable certificates of deposit, and asset-backed securities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Equity and investment fund shares
structure:Code.common:Description: Instruments representing a claim on the residual value of a corporation or investment fund, such as shares, stocks, participations, and depository receipts.

structure:Code.common:Name: Insurance, pensions, and standardized guarantee schemes
structure:Code.common:Description: Include life insurance and annuities entitlements which are assets of households; non-life insurance payable for claims not yet settled, or not yet presented; prepayment of non-life insurance premiums not yet used; pension fund reserves for offered pension schemes; and any other technical reserve.

structure:Code.common:Name: Loans
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial assets/liabilities created when creditors lend funds directly to debtors, and evidenced by documents that are not negotiable.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: All economic assets other than financial assets, which provide benefits to the institutional unit that owns them, such as real estate property for own-use, but do not represent claims on other institutional units.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonfinancial assets: Consumer durable goods
structure:Code.common:Description: Items which provide services to households over an extended period of time, such as cars, refrigerators, and washing machines.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonfinancial assets: other
structure:Code.common:Description: A broad category for nonfinancial assets not classified elsewhere (e.g., some intangibles, inventories, physical assets other than land/buildings).

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonfinancial assets: Real estate
structure:Code.common:Description: Refers to land and any permanent structures attached to it, such as buildings, houses, or commercial spaces.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross disposable income
structure:Code.common:Description: The remainder of the sum of the income received by the households, less tax on the income and wealth, social insurance contribution and current transfers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Current transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments received by households without any goods or services being provided in return, typically aimed at supporting income, welfare, and social security.

structure:Code.common:Name: Taxes including social security contributions and other current transfers
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes on income and wealth, contributions for social insurance, and other current transfers (e.g., payments of fines, penalties, and subscriptions to NPISHs).

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross disposable income: other
structure:Code.common:Description: Operating income from households' production activity within enterprises that are directly owned or controlled by members of the households.

structure:Code.common:Name: Property income receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Income receivable from financial and non-financial assets, such as interest, dividends, and rent income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Wages and salaries
structure:Code.common:Description: Compensation, in cash or kind, for employment.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Obligations of the entity to provide cash, financial instruments, or other items of economic value to other institutional units.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt
structure:Code.common:Description: The outstanding amount of current and non-contingent liabilities (such as loans, debt securities) that require payment of principal or interest in the future.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Miscellaneous liabilities, including accrued but unpaid taxes, dividends, social contributions and benefits, and other payables.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other debt instruments
structure:Code.common:Description: Debt liabilities or assets not counted under standard categories (such as bonds, loans, or money market instruments). Could include more unusual or residual debt-type claims/obligations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt-service payments (interest and principal)
structure:Code.common:Description: The interest and principal payable on outstanding debt liabilities during the reporting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt collateralized by real estate
structure:Code.common:Description: Encompasses all debt for which real estate is used as a form of collateral.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net worth
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between total assets and total liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Average capital and reserves
structure:Code.common:Description: The average value of capital and reserves from the start of the calendar year to the end of the current reporting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial derivatives
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial instruments that are linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, index, price, interest rate, or commodity, and through which specific financial risks can be traded in their own right in financial markets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other financial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Miscellaneous financial assets, including prepayments for services and other receivables.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trade credit
structure:Code.common:Description: Credit extended directly to purchasers of goods and services, advance payments for work that is in progress or is to be undertaken, and prepayments for goods and services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Annualized net income after taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: The estimated total net income after taxes that the institutional unit would earn over a year, calculated based on the amount earned and accumulated from the start of the calendar year to the end of the current reporting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonfinancial assets: Equipment
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of tangible assets that are used in the production of goods or provision of services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonfinancial assets: Inventories
structure:Code.common:Description: Inventories are materials and supplies held as inputs by producers, output as yet unsold, or products held by wholesale and retail traders.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonfinancial assets: Intellectual property products
structure:Code.common:Description: The value of results of research and development, mineral exploration and evaluation, computer software, data and databases, and entertainment, literary or artistic originals.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total liabilities and capital and reserves
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of all liabilities and capital and reserves.

structure:Code.common:Name: Capital and reserves
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between total assets and total liabilities in the balance sheet, and it represents the equity interest of the owners in an entity and is the amount available to absorb unidentified losses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cost of sales
structure:Code.common:Description: Includes personnel costs, costs of materials used in production, depreciation of installations and equipment, fixed and variable production overheads, rentals and royalties paid, distribution expenses, and other costs associated with production and sales.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total debt in foreign currency
structure:Code.common:Description: The part of nonfinancial corporations' total debt with principal and interest payments denominated in a currency other than the domestic currency, regardless of whether the creditor is resident or a nonresident.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total debt to nonresidents
structure:Code.common:Description: The outstanding amount of those actual current, and not contingent, liabilities that require payment of principal or interest by the debtor in the future and that are owed to nonresidents by resident nonfinancial corporations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Dividends payable
structure:Code.common:Description: The income to which shareholders become entitled, after other expenses have been met, as result of placing funds at the disposal of the corporation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Earnings before interest and tax
structure:Code.common:Description: The net operating income plus interest income plus other income (net) less interest income receivable from other nonfinancial corporations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Interest expenses
structure:Code.common:Description: Interest accrued and payable on debt instruments such as deposits, loans, debt securities, and other accounts payable.

structure:Code.common:Name: Interest income
structure:Code.common:Description: Income accrued on debt instruments (deposits, loans, debt securities, and other accounts receivable) including fees and commissions that form an integral part of the effective yield of the financial instruments, net of provisions for accrued interest.

structure:Code.common:Name: Interest and principal income receivable from other nonfinancial corporations
structure:Code.common:Description: The amount of interest income that is receivable from other nonfinancial corporations that are also in the reporting population.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net income after taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: The remainder of net income after deducting income tax.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net income before taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: The estimated total net income before tax that the institutional unit would earn over a year, calculated based on the amount earned and accumulated from the start of the calendar year to the end of the current reporting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other income (net)
structure:Code.common:Description: Includes rents, rentals, and royalties receivable (payable), income from holdings of equity, gains or losses on financial instruments and on the sales of fixed assets, and any amounts receivable (payable).

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial derivatives and employee stock options
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial instruments that are linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, index, price, interest rate, or commodity, and through which specific financial risks can be traded in their own right in financial markets. Employee stock options are contracts that give employees the right to purchase shares of their employer's stock at a predetermined price, usually as part of their compensation package.

structure:Code.common:Name: General and specific provisions
structure:Code.common:Description: General provisions are allowance set aside to cover anticipated future losses that are not yet specifically identified, while specific provisions are allowances for identified losses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net operating income
structure:Code.common:Description: Revenue from the sales of goods and services (excluding taxes on goods and services) less the cost of those sales.

structure:Code.common:Name: Retained earnings
structure:Code.common:Description: The net income after tax minus dividends payable, representing earnings retained in the entity for future use.

structure:Code.common:Name: Revenue from sales of goods and services (excluding indirect sales taxes)
structure:Code.common:Description: Gross revenue earned by the corporation from selling goods or providing services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Corporate income taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes accrued during the period and are related to the income, profit, and capital gains of the entity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Loans after specific provisions
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial assets created from lending funds directly to debtors, and evidenced by documents that are not negotiable [net of specific provisions].

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency loans
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans denominated in a currency other than the domestic currency.

structure:Code.common:Name: Noninterbank loans
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans granted to other sectors, other than deposit taking institutions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross loans
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial assets created from lending funds directly to debtors, and evidenced by documents that are not negotiable.

structure:Code.common:Name: Noninterbank loans
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans granted to other sectors, other than deposit taking institutions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Interbank loans
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans granted to other deposit takers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonperforming loans
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans for which (1) payments of interest or principal are past due by 90 days or more; or (2) interest payments equal to 90 days or more have been capitalized, refinanced, or rolled over; or (3)�evidence exists to reclassify them as nonperforming even in the absence of a 90-day past due payment, such as when the debtor files for bankruptcy.

structure:Code.common:Name: Commercial real estate loans
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of Loans collateralized by commercial real estate, loans to construction companies, and loans to companies active in the development of real estate.

structure:Code.common:Name: Residential real estate loans
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans collateralized by residential real estate (houses, apartments, other dwellings, and any associated land intended for occupancy by individual households).

structure:Code.common:Name: Specific provisions
structure:Code.common:Description: The outstanding amount of provisions made against the value of individual non-performing loans, collectively assessed groups of loans, and non-performing loans to other Deposit takers, in accordance with the national regulatory framework.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liquid assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets that are readily available to meet cash demands, including currency, deposits, and tradable securities that can be converted into cash with insignificant risk of change in value under normal business conditions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Risk-weighted assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Total of all on- and off-balance-sheet exposures weighted according to their perceived risk (credit, market, operational).

structure:Code.common:Name: Additional Tier 1 (AT1) capital less corresponding supervisory deductions
structure:Code.common:Description: Supervisory concept defined by Basel III, consisting of subordinated instruments with no maturity and neither secured nor covered by a guarantee of the issuer.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total balance sheet
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of nonfinancial and financial assets, representing the total resources owned by the institutional unit.

structure:Code.common:Name: Common equity Tier 1 capital less corresponding supervisory deductions
structure:Code.common:Description: Supervisory concept of the highest quality loss-absorbing capital defined by Basel III, comprising common shares, retained earnings and accumulated other comprehensive income, and other disclosed reserves, less corresponding supervisory deductions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Loan concentration by economic activity
structure:Code.common:Description: Deposit takers' lending to the largest three economic activities, as a proportion of their total gross loans to nonfinancial corporations.

structure:Code.common:Name: Credit to the private sector
structure:Code.common:Description: Gross loans extended to the private nonfinancial sector, plus debt securities issued by private nonfinancial corporations and held by Deposit takers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total regulatory capital
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 (when applicable) capital, after accounting for regulatory adjustments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tier 1 capital less corresponding supervisory deductions
structure:Code.common:Description: Comprises paid-up shares and common stock, and disclosed reserves that are available to meet claims against the deposit taker, with deductions such as goodwill. It is a supervisory concept defined by National regulation and based on Basel I, II, or III framework.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tier 2 capital less corresponding supervisory deductions
structure:Code.common:Description: Supervisory concept, introduced in Basel I, that includes financial instruments and reserves that can absorb losses but may not be permanent or fully reliable, such as subordinated debt, hybrid instruments, and general provisions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Tier 3 capital
structure:Code.common:Description: A Basel I/II concept, and consists of medium-term subordinated debt and is limited to 250 percent of the bank's Tier 1 capital.

structure:Code.common:Name: Noninterest expenses
structure:Code.common:Description: The operating expenses relating to the entity's ordinary business, such as personnel and other costs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Non-interest expenses: Other expenses
structure:Code.common:Description: Costs incurred by financial institutions that are not directly related to their core operations.�These can include administrative expenses, legal fees, and other miscellaneous costs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Non-interest Expenses: Personnel costs
structure:Code.common:Description: Total remuneration, in cash or in kind, payable to employees for work done during the accounting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Available amount of stable funding
structure:Code.common:Description: Supervisory concept defined by Basel III as the amount of capital and liability financing expected to be reliable sources of funds over a one-year time horizon under conditions of extended stress.

structure:Code.common:Name: Required amount of stable funding
structure:Code.common:Description: Supervisory concept defined by Basel III as the amount of stable funding needed to support deposit takers' assets and off-balance sheet activities over a one-year time horizon under conditions of extended stress.

structure:Code.common:Name: Highest interbank rate
structure:Code.common:Description: The highest interest rate charged on interbank loans. It is computed as the average of highest interbank rates on same maturity loans (daily or weekly) during the reporting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: High quality liquid assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Assets held by deposit takers to meet short-term liquidity needs during periods of financial stress.�These assets are characterized by their low risk, high credit quality, and ability to be quickly converted into cash with minimal loss in value, and the scope of these assets is defined by the national regulatory framework based on Basel III framework.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gross income
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of net income from insurance activity and other operating income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Interest income: Gross interest income
structure:Code.common:Description: Income accrued on debt instruments (deposits, loans, debt securities, and other accounts receivable) including fees and commissions that form an integral part of the effective yield of the financial instruments, gross of provisions for accrued interest.

structure:Code.common:Name: Interest income: Provisions for accrued interest on non-performing assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Interest accrued on nonperforming assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net interest income
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between interest income and interest expense.

structure:Code.common:Name: Noninterest income
structure:Code.common:Description: All other income received, including fees and commissions, gains and losses on financial instruments, prorated earnings, and other income; and excluding interest income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Noninterest income: Fees and commissions receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Income from provision of payment services, intermediary services, services related to transactions in securities, and asset management services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Noninterest income: Gains or losses on financial instruments
structure:Code.common:Description: Realized and unrealized gains and losses during the period on all financial instruments (assets and liabilities) that are held at Fair value through profit and loss on the balance sheet.

structure:Code.common:Name: Noninterest income: other income
structure:Code.common:Description: Includes declared dividend receivable, gains or losses on sale of fixed assets, rental and royalty income receivable, and any amounts receivable from compensation for damage or injury.

structure:Code.common:Name: Noninterest income: Prorated earnings
structure:Code.common:Description: Proportion of net income after tax from associates, unconsolidated subsidiaries, reverse equity investments, and�for domestic-based data�foreign branches.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities denominated in a currency other than the domestic currency.

structure:Code.common:Name: Short term liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities that are due on demand or within three months or less.

structure:Code.common:Name: Interbank deposits
structure:Code.common:Description: Deposits from other deposit takers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Customer deposits
structure:Code.common:Description: Deposits placed by residents or nonresidents, except those placed by (resident and nonresident) financial corporations, central governments, and central banks.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other currency and deposits
structure:Code.common:Description: Currency and deposit instruments not included in typical transferable or broad money categories (possibly foreign-currency deposits or specialized deposit-like instruments).

structure:Code.common:Name: Lowest interbank rate
structure:Code.common:Description: The lowest interest rate charged on interbank loans. It is computed as the average of lowest interbank rates on same maturity loans (daily or weekly) during the reporting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other comprehensive income (loss) net of tax
structure:Code.common:Description: Items not recognized in profit or loss, such as unrealized gains or losses on financial assets and foreign currency translation adjustments, after deducting the applicable tax.

structure:Code.common:Name: General and other provisions
structure:Code.common:Description: Provisions set aside to cover anticipated future losses that are not yet specifically identified.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total net open position in foreign currency
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of the net position of on-balance sheet foreign currency debt instruments, net positions in financial derivatives, on-balance sheet holdings of foreign currency equity assets, and net position in foreign currency off-balance sheet items.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net open position in foreign currency for on-balance-sheet items
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of the net position of on-balance sheet foreign currency debt instruments, net positions in financial derivatives, and on-balance sheet holdings of foreign currency equity assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Provisions (net)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net change in allowances for losses on all financial assets that are within the scope of IFRS 9, to reflect increase in expected credit loss (expense) or decreases in expected credit loss (income).

structure:Code.common:Name: Provisions (net): Loan loss provisions
structure:Code.common:Description: Net new allowances for Loan losses during the reporting period to reflect increase in expected credit loss (expense) or decreases in expected credit loss (income).

structure:Code.common:Name: Provisions (net): Other financial asset provisions
structure:Code.common:Description: Expense on Expected Credit Loss allowance on any other Financial assets, other than loans, that are within the scope of IFRS9.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reference deposit rate
structure:Code.common:Description: The weighted average interest rate on loans / deposits during the period, excluding interest charged on loans / deposits between deposit takers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reference lending rate
structure:Code.common:Description: Series for further analysis of the balance sheet, Reference lending rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other supervisory deductions
structure:Code.common:Description: Other adjustments to account for specific regulatory requirements or risks that are not covered by standard capital deductions, to buttress the quality of capital. As defined by National regulatory framework, based on the BCBS's Basel I, II or III framework.

structure:Code.common:Name: Basel III total exposure measure
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of a deposit taker's on-balance sheet exposures, derivative exposures, securities financing transaction exposures, and off-balance sheet items.

structure:Code.common:Name: Income tax
structure:Code.common:Description: Taxes accrued during the period and are related to the income, profit, and capital gains of the entity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total net cash outflows over the next 30 calendar days
structure:Code.common:Description: Supervisory concept defined in Basel III as the total expected cash outflows minus the total expected cash inflows in the specified stress scenario for the subsequent 30 calendar days.

structure:Code.common:Name: Value of large exposures
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of all exposure values of a deposit taker to a counterparty or to a group of connected counterparties, if it is equal to or above 10 percent of the deposit takers' eligible capital base define by the Regulatory framework.

structure:Code.common:Name: Average total assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The average value of total assets from the start of the calendar year to the end of the current reporting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reinsurance claims
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims that Insurance corporations have on reinsurers, being the reinsurers' obligation to reimburse the insurance company for a portion of the claims that the insurance company has paid to its policyholders.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reinsurance claims: Reinsurance recoverable
structure:Code.common:Description: Total expected recoveries from reinsurers for covered losses - includes both settled but unpaid amounts and anticipated future claim reimbursements.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reinsurance claims: Reinsurance receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Amounts owed to the insurer by reinsurers for claims already paid (or recognized) by the ceding insurer. Essentially short-term receivables from the reinsurer.

structure:Code.common:Name: Annualized net income before taxes
structure:Code.common:Description: The estimated total net income before tax that the institutional unit would earn over a year, calculated based on the amount earned and accumulated from the start of the calendar year to the end of the current reporting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonfinancial assets: Property for investment
structure:Code.common:Description: Property, such as real estate, held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation, or both.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonfinancial assets: Property for own use
structure:Code.common:Description: Property, such as real estate, that is occupied by the owner or lessee for their own business or personal use.

structure:Code.common:Name: Claims incurred net of reinsurance
structure:Code.common:Description: Total claims expenses incurred by Insurance corporations during the reporting period, after deducting the portion of these claims that is recoverable from reinsurers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Claims incurred, net of reinsurance: Changes in reserves for claims outstanding
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the reserves that Insurance corporations hold to cover claims that have been reported but not yet settled, as well as claims that have been incurred but not yet reported.

structure:Code.common:Name: Claims incurred, net of reinsurance: Gross claim payments
structure:Code.common:Description: Total amount paid by Insurance corporations to policyholders or beneficiaries for claims incurred during a specific period, before deducting any reinsurance recoveries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Claims incurred, net of reinsurance: Reinsurers' share of gross claim payments
structure:Code.common:Description: The portion of the total claim payments made by Insurance corporations that is recoverable from reinsurers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Claims incurred, net of reinsurance: Transfer of premium reserves to other companies
structure:Code.common:Description: Reserves on existing insurance policies that are transferred, along with the associated insurance policies, between insurance companies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gain/losses due to revaluations of financial assets/liabilities
structure:Code.common:Description: Realized and unrealized gains and losses during the period on all financial instruments (assets and liabilities) that are held at Fair value through profit and loss on the balance sheet.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income (net): From financial investments
structure:Code.common:Description: Net returns on the entity's financial investment portfolio (e.g., bond interest, dividends, realized gains/losses), minus associated investment expenses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income (net): Interest cost
structure:Code.common:Description: The interest expense portion of net investment income i.e., the cost of funds used to finance the investment portfolio or other liabilities. This amount reduces overall reported investment income.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income (net): From other investments
structure:Code.common:Description: Net income from nonfinancial or miscellaneous investments (e.g., real estate, equity in nonfinancial companies), excluding standard financial instruments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Insurance, pensions, and standardized guarantee schemes: Net equity of households in life insurance reserves
structure:Code.common:Description: Households' accumulated claims on life insurers - essentially the reserves life insurers hold for policyholders (households), net of liabilities and expenses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Insurance, pensions, and standardized guarantee schemes: Other technical provisions
structure:Code.common:Description: Other insurance liabilities beyond life and pension entitlements (e.g., reserves for nonlife policies, unearned premiums, outstanding claims). Ensures sufficient funding for future obligations not covered by standard life or pension reserves.

structure:Code.common:Name: Insurance, pensions, and standardized guarantee schemes: Pension fund reserves
structure:Code.common:Description: The reserves of pension schemes needed to meet current and future pension obligations to participants. Represents the liabilities of pension funds to their beneficiaries.

structure:Code.common:Name: Insurance, pensions, and standardized guarantee schemes: Prepayment of insurance premiums and insurance payable
structure:Code.common:Description: Includes prepayments of insurance premiums not yet earned (unearned premium reserves) and any insurance payables (due to policyholders or for claims).

structure:Code.common:Name: Net income from insurance activity
structure:Code.common:Description: Total income generated from Insurance corporations' core operations, including premiums earned, investment income, and other related revenues, minus the expenses incurred from claims, commissions, and other operational costs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income (net)
structure:Code.common:Description: Income earned from holdings of financial instruments and nonfinancial assets, associated with both unit-linked and non-unit-linked products; net of interest cost on liabilities, own property management costs, and the income on unit-linked products passed on to policyholders.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net change in technical reserves for future claims
structure:Code.common:Description: Adjustments made to the reserves that Insurance corporations hold to cover claims, reflecting changes in the estimated liabilities for claims that have been reported but not yet settled, as well as claims that have been incurred but not yet reported.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other operating expenses
structure:Code.common:Description: Expenses on personnel, underwriting, depreciation of non-financial assets, and any other operating costs not related to claims or investments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other operating expenses: Real estate expenses or nonfinancial assets depreciation
structure:Code.common:Description: Costs associated with owning, operating, and maintaining real estate properties, as well as the depreciation of nonfinancial assets during the period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other operating expenses: Underwriting expenses
structure:Code.common:Description: Costs incurred by Insurance corporations during the evaluation, selection, and issuance of insurance policies, including commissions paid to agents and brokers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other operating income
structure:Code.common:Description: Sum of commissions received, real estate income, and other income, which are not related to core activity.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other operating income: Commissions received
structure:Code.common:Description: Income earned from providing services such as brokerage, underwriting, and advisory services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other operating income: Gains and losses from sales of fixed assets
structure:Code.common:Description: The financial results from selling fixed assets, such as property, plant, and equipment - calculated as the difference between the sale proceeds and the book value of the assets sold.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other operating income: Other income
structure:Code.common:Description: Includes declared dividend receivable, royalty income receivable, and any amounts receivable from compensation for damage or injury.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other operating income: Real estate income
structure:Code.common:Description: Income generated from the ownership, leasing, and management of real estate properties.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums earned net of reinsurance
structure:Code.common:Description: Total premiums received by Insurance corporations from policyholders during the reporting period, after deducting reinsurance premiums and other adjustments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums earned net of reinsurance: Gross premium earned
structure:Code.common:Description: Total premiums received by Insurance corporations from policyholders during a specific period, before deducting reinsurance premiums and other adjustments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums earned net of reinsurance: Reinsurers' share of gross premiums earned
structure:Code.common:Description: The portion of gross premium earned by Insurance corporations that is ceded or paid to reinsurers, to transfer part of the risk to the reinsurers.

structure:Code.common:Name: Premiums earned net of reinsurance: Transfer of premium reserves from other companies
structure:Code.common:Description: Reserves on existing insurance policies that are transferred, along with the associated insurance policies, between insurance companies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Pension benefit surplus
structure:Code.common:Description: The surplus of a pension fund's assets over its actuarially determined liabilities, implying assets exceed projected obligations for participants.

structure:Code.common:Name: Contributions receivable
structure:Code.common:Description: Contributions receivable are amounts an insurer or pension fund expects to receive from plan sponsors, employers, or participants for coverage or benefits that have already been accrued but not yet paid. In other words, they represent an asset (a claim) for contributions that have been invoiced or contractually earned but remain outstanding at the reporting date.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment expense
structure:Code.common:Description: The expenses incurred on managing investments and the tax on the return on investments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment expense: Investment management expenses
structure:Code.common:Description: Payments to fund managers, custodians, banks, accountants, lawyers, for managing the pension fund's investments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment expense: Taxation on investments
structure:Code.common:Description: The tax on the return on investments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Estimated pension payments in the next 12 months
structure:Code.common:Description: The sum of the actuarially expected payments to beneficiaries by pension funds during the next year.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income: Net change in fair value of investments
structure:Code.common:Description: The gain/loss in the market value of investments over a specific period, due to factors (such as market prices and interest rates) affecting the value of the investments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income: Interest income
structure:Code.common:Description: Income that accrues on debt instruments such as deposits, loans, debt securities, and other accounts receivable. It also includes fees and commissions that are an integral part of the effective yield of a financial instrument.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income: Other income from investments
structure:Code.common:Description: Includes capital gains on equity and income from investments in real estate property.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income
structure:Code.common:Description: Composed of interest income on financial instruments, other income on financial instruments (e.g., capital gains), income from investments in property, and the net change in the fair value of investments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net equity of households in pension fund reserves
structure:Code.common:Description: The amount of financial claims both existing and future that pensioners hold against the pension funds to pay pensions or other entitlements such as health benefits.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net equity of households in pension fund reserves: Defined benefit
structure:Code.common:Description: Households' claims under defined benefit pension schemes, where retirement benefits depend on a formula (e.g., salary and service). Reflects the present value of promised benefits (less any plan liabilities).

structure:Code.common:Name: Net equity of households in pension fund reserves: Defined contribution
structure:Code.common:Description: The accumulated account balances to which households are entitled under defined contribution pension plans, where benefits depend on contributions plus investment returns.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net equity of households in pension fund reserves: Hybrid schemes
structure:Code.common:Description: Households' claims in hybrid pension plans, which combine features of both defined benefit and defined contribution systems.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net actuarial gains/losses
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between the long-term estimates and the actual experiences of the pension plan assets and liabilities, arising from changes in actuarial assumptions, during the reporting period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net investment income
structure:Code.common:Description: Investment income minus investment expenses.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other income
structure:Code.common:Description: Any income not captured under net premiums or investment income. Could include fee/commission revenues or other miscellaneous operating gains.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total administrative expenses
structure:Code.common:Description: The costs associated with the overall administration of the pension fund, including expenses for record-keeping, accounting services, and regulatory compliance.

structure:Code.common:Name: Noninterest expenses and provisions
structure:Code.common:Description: The operating expenses relating to the entity's ordinary business, such as personnel costs, expenses on property and equipment, purchase of goods and services, royalties paid, taxes other than income taxes, fines and penalties imposed on the entity. Provisions are the allowances for loss on financial instruments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment fund shares issued
structure:Code.common:Description: Comprise shares or units issued by money market funds, representing a claim on the value of collective investment undertakings.

structure:Code.common:Name: Sectoral distribution of investments
structure:Code.common:Description: Percentage of the Money market funds' investments in a given sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total financial system assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Sum of assets of the financial institutions in the financial system, excluding the central bank.

structure:Code.common:Name: Geographic distribution of loans: Emerging Market and Developing Economies
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans to non-residents domiciled in Emerging Market and Developing Economies, as a percentage of total loans.

structure:Code.common:Name: Geographic distribution of loans: Emerging and Developing Europe
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans to non-residents domiciled in Emerging and Developing Europe, as a percentage of total loans.

structure:Code.common:Name: Geographic distribution of loans: Latin America and the Caribbean
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans to non-residents domiciled in Latin America and the Caribbean, as a percentage of total loans.

structure:Code.common:Name: Geographic distribution of loans: Advanced Economies
structure:Code.common:Description: Lending to Advanced economies as a percentage to total loans.

structure:Code.common:Name: Geographic distribution of loans: Emerging and Developing Asia
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans to non-residents domiciled in Emerging and Developing Asia, as a percentage of total loans.

structure:Code.common:Name: Geographic distribution of loans: Domestic Economies
structure:Code.common:Description: Lending to domestic sectors as a percentage to total loans.

structure:Code.common:Name: Geographic distribution of loans: Middle East and Central Asia
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans to non-residents domiciled in Middle East and Central Asia, as a percentage of total loans.

structure:Code.common:Name: Geographic distribution of loans: Sub-Saharan Africa
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans to non-residents domiciled in Sub-Saharan Africa, as a percentage of total loans.

structure:Code.common:Name: Loans to Advanced Economies
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans extended to non-residents domiciled in Advanced Economies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Loans to Latin America and the Caribbean
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans extended to non-residents domiciled in Latin America and the Caribbean.

structure:Code.common:Name: Loans to Emerging and Developing Europe
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans extended to non-residents domiciled in Emerging and Developing Europe.

structure:Code.common:Name: Loans to Emerging Market and Developing Economies
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans extended to non-residents domiciled in Emerging Market and Developing Economies.

structure:Code.common:Name: Loans to Middle East and Central Asia
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans extended to non-residents domiciled in Middle East and Central Asia.

structure:Code.common:Name: Loans to Sub-Saharan Africa
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans extended to non-residents domiciled in Sub-Saharan Africa.

structure:Code.common:Name: Loans to Emerging and Developing Asia
structure:Code.common:Description: Loans extended to non-residents domiciled in Emerging and Developing Asia.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other operating expenses: Other expenses
structure:Code.common:Description: Costs incurred by the institutional units that are not directly related to their core operations.�These can include administrative expenses, legal fees, and other miscellaneous costs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other operating expenses: Personnel costs
structure:Code.common:Description: Total remuneration, in cash or in kind, payable to employees for work done during the accounting period.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Frequency
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This code list provides a set of values indicating the "frequency" of the data (e.g. weekly, monthly, quarterly). The concept “frequency” may refer to various stages in the production process, e.g. data collection or data dissemination. For example, a time series could be disseminated at annual frequency but the underlying data are compiled monthly. The code list is applicable for all different uses of "frequency". This code list was formally adopted on 4 December 2013. More information about and supporting material for this code list and SDMX code lists in general (e.g. list of generic codes for expressing general concepts like "Total", "Unknown", etc.; syntaxes for the creation of further codes; general guidelines for the creation of SDMX code lists) can be found at this address: https://sdmx.org/?page_id=4345.

structure:Code.common:Name: Semimonthly

structure:Code.common:Name: Three times a month
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated three times a month.

structure:Code.common:Name: Biweekly
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated every two weeks.

structure:Code.common:Name: Triweekly
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated every three weeks.

structure:Code.common:Name: Four-weekly
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated every four weeks.

structure:Code.common:Name: Semiweekly
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated twice a week.

structure:Code.common:Name: Three times a week
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated three times a week.

structure:Code.common:Name: Twice a day
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated twice a day.

structure:Code.common:Name: Hourly
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated every hour.

structure:Code.common:Name: Bihourly
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated every two hours.

structure:Code.common:Name: Trihourly
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used for data collected or disseminated every three hours.

structure:Code.common:Name: Daily – business week
structure:Code.common:Description: Similar to "daily", however there are no observations for Saturdays and Sundays (so, neither “missing values” nor “numeric values” should be provided for Saturday and Sunday)

structure:Code.common:Name: Minutely
structure:Code.common:Description: While N denotes "minutely", usually, there may be no observations every minute (for several series the frequency is usually "irregular" within a day/days). And though observations may be sparse (not collected or disseminated every minute), missing values do not need to be given for the minutes when no observations exist: in any case the time stamp determines when an observation is observed.

structure:Code.common:Name: Irregular
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used with irregular time series that stores data for a sequence of arbitrary timepoints. Irregular time series are appropriate when the data arrives unpredictably, such as when the application records every stock trade or when random events are recorded (the interval between each element can be a different length)

structure:Code.common:Name: Occasional annual
structure:Code.common:Description: The event occurs occasionally with an infrequent update that could span from 1 year to several years between events. It implies a survey that experiences a gap for several years prior to the next survey update (this is commonly linked to funding available to run a specific survey (i.e. health surveys), whereas a regular annual survey refers typically to ‘programs’ that are funded regularly and fall under the Statistics Act, and therefore never experience a gap)

structure:Code.common:Name: Occasional monthly
structure:Code.common:Description: The event occurs occasionally with an infrequent update that could span from 1 month to several months between events. It implies a survey that experiences a gap for several months prior to the next survey update.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used when the qualitative or quantitative values that a variable takes in a data set is associated to multiple occurrences with frequency other than the already defined ones (for example every 5 hours and 32 minutes etc.)

structure:Code.common:Name: Unspecified
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used when a set of values are reported within a time range but not associated to sub ranges. Often this could happen in case of missing or sparse information. (Let’s say we have two observations for 2020 but we do not know if they are part of a monthly reporting or quarterly reporting)

structure:Code.common:Name: Not applicable
structure:Code.common:Description: To be used when the qualitative or quantitative values that a variable takes in a data set is not associated to multiple occurrences (only single occurrence exists) one can use the _Z as frequency.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Derivation Type
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist identifies the specific method used to derive a new data element or indicator from source data, such as raw data, IMF staff calculations, IMF staff estimates, or IMF staff projections.

structure:Code.common:Name: Staff estimates using group mean imputation methods
structure:Code.common:Description: Staff estimates using group mean imputation methods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Staff estimates using historical imputation methods
structure:Code.common:Description: Staff estimates using historical imputation methods.

structure:Code.common:Name: Raw data (no derivation)
structure:Code.common:Description: Non-transformed data (also called original data) refers to data in its original form, before any mathematical or statistical operations have been applied to change its values or distribution.

structure:Code.common:Name: IMF Staff calculations (derived value)
structure:Code.common:Description: Data that results from direct calculations or transformations performed on raw data by IMF staff. These calculations are usually straightforward and transparent, with the published numbers easily traceable back to the source data.

structure:Code.common:Name: IMF Staff calculations (derived from counterpart data)
structure:Code.common:Description: Data resulting from direct application of counterpart data by IMF staff to the official information reported by other countries.

structure:Code.common:Name: IMF Staff estimates
structure:Code.common:Description: Data derived through calculations or transformations on available source data, where some necessary information might be missing. In these cases, IMF staff uses estimates to fill in the gaps and produce the published numbers.

structure:Code.common:Name: IMF Staff projections
structure:Code.common:Description: Forecasts of future values for a time series, constructed using various techniques such as statistical modeling, trend analysis, and expert judgment. These projections are based on historical data, current economic conditions, and other relevant factors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Mixed-type data
structure:Code.common:Description: Data that combines both raw and derived data. This could occur when some components of a dataset are directly reported while others are calculated or estimated.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reported official data
structure:Code.common:Description: Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities without any modifications or adjustments made by IMF staff.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reported official data converted to US dollar
structure:Code.common:Description: Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities in a country's domestic currency, which IMF staff then converts to US dollars using appropriate exchange rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Adjusted using Fund records
structure:Code.common:Description: Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities that has that have been adjusted using internal IMF records.

structure:Code.common:Name: Third party data
structure:Code.common:Description: Third party data.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Frequency
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This code list provides a set of values indicating the "frequency" of the data (e.g. weekly, monthly, quarterly). The concept “frequency” may refer to various stages in the production process, e.g. data collection or data dissemination. For example, a time series could be disseminated at annual frequency but the underlying data are compiled monthly. The code list is applicable for all different uses of "frequency". This code list was formally adopted on 4 December 2013. More information about and supporting material for this code list and SDMX code lists in general (e.g. list of generic codes for expressing general concepts like "Total", "Unknown", etc.; syntaxes for the creation of further codes; general guidelines for the creation of SDMX code lists) can be found at this address: https://sdmx.org/?page_id=4345.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Unit of Measure
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist represents the standard unit used to quantify a particular data element or indicator. It encompasses various units, including currency, physical units, percentages, and other standardized measures.

structure:Code.common:Name: 1000 hectares
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of area equal to 1,000 hectares (10,000,000 square meters).

structure:Code.common:Name: Barrel
structure:Code.common:Description: Unit of volume for crude oil and other petroleum products. Equal to 42 US gallons.

structure:Code.common:Name: Barrels per day
structure:Code.common:Description: Unit of measurement used in the oil and gas industry to describe the rate of production or consumption of petroleum products.

structure:Code.common:Name: Basis points
structure:Code.common:Description: Basis points refers to hundredths of 1 percentage point.

structure:Code.common:Name: Carat
structure:Code.common:Description: The carat is a unit of mass equal to 200 mg, used for measuring gemstones and pearls. Also used to indicate the proportion of gold in an alloy out of 24 parts (e.g., 18K gold is 18/24 parts gold).

structure:Code.common:Name: Centimeter
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of length in the metric system, equal to one hundredth of a meter.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cubic meter
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of volume equal to a cube one meter long on each side.

structure:Code.common:Name: Days
structure:Code.common:Description: A period of twenty-four hours as a unit of time.

structure:Code.common:Name: Degrees Celsius
structure:Code.common:Description: The degree Celsius (symbol: °C) can refer to a specific point on the Celsius temperature scale or to a difference or range between two temperatures.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gallon
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of liquid capacity equal to 3.79 liters.

structure:Code.common:Name: Gigawatt hours
structure:Code.common:Description: Gigawatt hours (GWh) is a unit of energy representing one billion watt hours.

structure:Code.common:Name: Hectare
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of area equal to 10,000 square meters.

structure:Code.common:Name: Hours
structure:Code.common:Description: A period of time equal to a twenty-fourth part of a day and night.

structure:Code.common:Name: US dollar index
structure:Code.common:Description: A value expressed in US dollar that is derived from an index computation.

structure:Code.common:Name: Index
structure:Code.common:Description: A statistical measure that expresses the relative change in a variable in the current period compared to the index reference period.

structure:Code.common:Name: Kilogram
structure:Code.common:Description: The base unit of mass in the International System of Units (SI).

structure:Code.common:Name: Kilometer
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of length in the metric system, equal to one thousand meters.

structure:Code.common:Name: Kiloton of CO₂ equivalent
structure:Code.common:Description: Measurement of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Kilowatt hour
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of energy equal to one kilowatt of power expended for one hour.

structure:Code.common:Name: Liter
structure:Code.common:Description: A metric unit of capacity, equal to 1,000 cubic centimeters.

structure:Code.common:Name: Long ton
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of weight equal to 2,240 pounds (1,016.0 kg).

structure:Code.common:Name: Unitless
structure:Code.common:Description: A quantity that has no physical unit of measurement, typically because it represents a ratio, proportion, index.

structure:Code.common:Name: Megawatt
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of power equal to one million watts.

structure:Code.common:Name: Meter
structure:Code.common:Description: The base unit of length in the International System of Units (SI).

structure:Code.common:Name: Metric ton
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of weight equal to 1,000 kilograms (2,204.6 pounds).

structure:Code.common:Name: Metric ton of CO₂
structure:Code.common:Description: Measurement of carbon dioxide emissions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Metric ton of CO₂ equivalent
structure:Code.common:Description: A metric measure used to compare the emissions from various greenhouse gases on the basis of their global-warming potential. 1

structure:Code.common:Name: Millimeter
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of length in the metric system, equal to one thousandth of a meter.

structure:Code.common:Name: Millions of metric tonnes
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of weight equal to one million metric tons.

structure:Code.common:Name: Months
structure:Code.common:Description: Each of the twelve named periods into which a year is divided.

structure:Code.common:Name: Number
structure:Code.common:Description: A mathematical object used to count, measure, and label.

structure:Code.common:Name: Parts per million
structure:Code.common:Description: A measure of concentration, indicating one part per million of a substance in a solution.

structure:Code.common:Name: Per US dollar
structure:Code.common:Description: Indicates a rate or quantity relative to one US dollar.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percent
structure:Code.common:Description: A ratio expressed as a fraction of 100.

structure:Code.common:Name: Percentage points
structure:Code.common:Description: The difference between two percentages.

structure:Code.common:Name: Persons
structure:Code.common:Description: Individuals.

structure:Code.common:Name: Pound
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of weight equal to 16 ounces (0.4536 kg).

structure:Code.common:Name: Short ton
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of weight equal to 2,000 pounds (907.18 kg).

structure:Code.common:Name: Square kilometer
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of area equal to a square that is one kilometer long on each side.

structure:Code.common:Name: Square meter
structure:Code.common:Description: The unit of area in the International System of Units (SI).

structure:Code.common:Name: Thousand cubic feet
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of volume equal to one thousand cubic feet of gas.

structure:Code.common:Name: Thousand cubic meters
structure:Code.common:Description: A unit of volume equal to one thousand cubic meters.

structure:Code.common:Name: Number of tourist nights
structure:Code.common:Description: The number of nights spent by tourists at a destination.

structure:Code.common:Name: Visitors
structure:Code.common:Description: People visiting a person, place, or event.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fine troy ounces
structure:Code.common:Description: Measurement of volume in millions of troy ounces of precious metals.

structure:Code.common:Name: Fine troy ounces of gold bullion

structure:Code.common:Name: Coarse particle, 99.2%
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to a material with a specific particle size distribution where 99.2% of the particles are larger than a certain size threshold, indicating a coarse or granular material. The exact size threshold would depend on the context and the specific material being described.

structure:Code.common:Name: Battery Grade, 99%
structure:Code.common:Description: This refers to a material or substance that has a purity level of 99% and is suitable for use in batteries. The term "Battery Grade" indicates that the material meets the specific quality and performance requirements for battery applications, such as electrochemical stability, high energy density, and long cycle life.

structure:Code.common:Name: Cost, insurance, and freight Northwest Europe
structure:Code.common:Description: Cost, Insurance, and Freight Northwest Europe (CIF NWE) is a pricing term used in the oil and petroleum industry. It indicates that the seller is responsible for the costs, insurance, and freight of delivering the product to a port in Northwest Europe assumes responsibility for the goods once they are loaded onto the ship at the port of origin. NEW likely refers to a specific geographic region or port, but without further context, it's difficult to be certain.
